body:
Global crypto markets closed Tuesday in cautious recovery mode, with the total market cap settling at $2.28T, up +0.62% on the day. Volume came in at $53.7B, respectable but not enough to signal a decisive shift in character. The Fear and Greed index moved from 31 yesterday to 41 today, still firmly in Fear territory but off the floor, which suggests some marginal de-risking fatigue without any genuine conviction returning. BTC dominance held at 56.6%, with ETH dominance at 10.1%, and the spread between the two reflects a market where capital is parking in the relative safety of the largest cap rather than rotating into risk. The session had a bifurcated feel: BTC grinded higher while a meaningful cohort of altcoins continued bleeding, keeping mood cautious despite the green headline number.

Bitcoin traded at $64,216 at the time of writing, up +1.20% over the prior 24 hours and essentially flat over 7 days at +0.50%, with $21.54B in volume. The move above $64,000 is the headline, and it matters symbolically, but CoinDesk flagged the specific price level around here as where leveraged longs become vulnerable to a flush — meaning the market is acutely aware that this is not clean air above. The 1-hour print of +0.10% suggests momentum has stalled after the initial push. Bulls need to see a convincing hold and expansion through current levels to neutralize that liquidation risk narrative; a rejection here that puts $62,000 back in play would be the path of most pain for late longs and would likely drag the broader market cap back toward $2.2T. Watch the $64,000 handle as the immediate pivot.

Ethereum at $1,897.94 lagged BTC meaningfully on the day, up only +0.20% in 24 hours though the 7-day print of +1.50% is the strongest of the cohort outside of LINK. The ETH/BTC ratio compression is notable and consistent with the dominance data. Elsewhere the altcoin picture was messy. LINK was the standout, up +12.30% over 7 days with $0.24B in volume, though the 24-hour gain was a modest +0.30%, suggesting the weekly move is maturing. SOL added +0.70% on the day at $75.98 and looks the most constructive of the mid-caps. UNI gained +0.80% in 24 hours but is nursing a brutal -18.00% 7-day loss, making today's bounce look more like relief than reversal. XRP dropped below the psychologically important $1.00 level, sitting at $0.995881 with a -0.40% daily and -1.20% 7-day decline — this despite South Korea's Jeonbuk Bank announcing adoption of Ripple Payments, which underscores how little utility narratives are moving price in the current environment. DOT and ADA were the session's clearest underperformers, off -3.30% and -1.90% respectively, with DOT down -8.10% over the week and ADA -7.50%, both printing the kind of sustained drawdown that points to continued capital flight from lower-liquidity layer-1s.

On the macro side, sentiment remains risk-averse across asset classes and crypto is reflecting that. The Fear and Greed reading of 41 tells you positioning is not extended, but it also tells you fresh capital is not coming in at scale. Regulatory noise is a persistent headwind: US authorities are pressing charges against an alleged $165M Ponzi mastermind after extradition from Fiji, which keeps enforcement headlines hot. On the protocol side, the Ethereum Foundation issued a warning that certain developer tools may break with the Glamsterdam upgrade, an unhelpful addition to the ETH narrative at a moment when the asset needs positive catalysts. Kraken parent Payward joining Anthropic's Project Glasswing for AI security is an interesting institutional signal but not a near-term price driver. Monad's reported offer to buy out early investors at up to $60 million — with almost universal rejection according to CoinDesk — is a notable data point on private market sentiment and conviction among insiders in the Ethereum-competitor space.

Looking ahead, the immediate question for BTC is whether it can consolidate above $64,000 or whether the leveraged long overhang forces a retest of lower support. A clean daily close above this level with expanding volume would shift the near-term bias constructively; a failure here with any macro catalyst — whether a hotter-than-expected Fed speaker, renewed geopolitical escalation, or a regulatory headline — could accelerate a move back into the low $60,000s quickly. For ETH, the Glamsterdam uncertainty is worth monitoring; developer confidence matters for on-chain activity and fee revenue narratives. XRP holding or reclaiming $1.00 is the clearest binary to watch in altcoins. Broader risk appetite, particularly how traditional equity markets absorb any rate-related news flow this week, will set the ceiling for how far crypto can extend any recovery. The setup right now is fragile: improved from yesterday, but one adverse catalyst away from re-testing the Fear index lows.
